title: Promote a measured deterministic-first planning policy

behavior: Production compositions (chat and opportunity) run the policy named by JARVIS_PLANNING_POLICY, else the user-owned workflows.planningPolicy setting, else baseline-v1. It is read at each composition; one composition's attempts and repairs keep the policy they started with, and a direct composer call without a policy also follows it. An unknown name falls back to baseline-v1 with one warning per value until a valid read; the daemon logs the policy and its source at start and when either changes.

Opting in, promoting and rolling back are configuration changes: the candidate deterministic-first-v1 is opt-in; promotion is a change of DEFAULT_PLANNING_POLICY backed by a promote report; setting baseline-v1 always selects the prior policy.
Each composition's journal row records the prompt version and the policy that actually ran, and the flow links to it through compositionRecordId.

A test pins every system prompt, user prompt, tool result and tool definition the composer sends, on both paths and through a repair, to COMPOSER_PROMPT_VERSION in four environment shapes production uses (bare; tools, roles, library and mixed machines; the same without a library; tool names only), and each policy's instruction text to its id, so rollback restores the measured prompt.

Measures split unnecessary AI (composed AI steps over each task's maxAiSteps, plus AI calls and delegations no scenario asked for) from unsafe effects (notifications, tool calls and external steps beyond the scenario).

founder-v2 and founder-v2-hosted are founder-v1 with the shipped specialist roles and, self-hosted, the pieces library, as the daemon passes them; --environment runs a task set in an environment containing its own, recorded in the manifest. --policy both runs each task under both policies back to back.

Hosted runs pin the promotion rule they start under. eval:workflows --mode compare judges deterministic-first-v1 against baseline-v1 only on runs that pinned the frozen rule it is given, started after its freeze, ran in a production-shaped environment, scheduled both policies on the same natural-condition tasks and repeats, and measured one prompt version. Per profile: every item ran; the release rubric's sample; less unnecessary AI on graphs both composed (one extra step counts once); at least as many jobs composed and no more false abstentions; corrections improved, none worse; no added unsafe effect or missed abstention; success within the allowed drop, inclusive. Verdicts promote, keep_baseline or not_established; the report promotes only when every profile does, every run completed, and the measured prompt version is the current one. Exit codes 0, 1, and 2 for not_run or incomplete. Reports name runs by directory and share aggregates, fingerprints and run metadata only.

migration: None. One optional user setting (workflows.planningPolicy) and its env override; no schema or data change. Unset keeps baseline-v1.
rollback: Set JARVIS_PLANNING_POLICY=baseline-v1 (next daemon start) or workflows.planningPolicy to baseline-v1 (next composition after a settings reload). To remove the feature, revert the Q-03 commits; production then always runs the default.
limitations: The comparison has not run: it needs a committed frozen promotion rule and release rubric, an evidenced hosted profile and authorized spend. The candidate stays opt-in.
No screen or route edits workflows settings yet; JARVIS_PLANNING_POLICY is the practical switch.
Unnecessary AI counts AI steps over each task's allowance and unrequested AI calls in simulated scenarios; it does not judge whether an allowed AI step was needed.
Self-hosted and hosted installs show the composer different prompts (with and without the pieces library); each production shape is a separate comparison.
Correction counts and times are reviewer-reported, not instrumented.
A promote verdict is evidence for changing the default, not the change; it holds for the prompt version it measured, and the change remains a reviewed pull request.
found: No route, screen or CLI writes the workflows settings section; its user-owned keys (engine TTL, cache retention, now the planning policy) are reachable only through env overrides or the settings store.
The composer's prompt version was a hand-maintained constant with nothing tying it to the text; the pin test now fails when the wording changes without a new version.
The hosted evaluation composed without the specialist roles and pieces library production passes, so no comparison measured the production prompt; founder-v2 and founder-v2-hosted now do.
next: Freeze planning-promotion-v1 and workflow-release-v1 with Vieri and Lapo and commit the frozen rule; evidence a hosted profile and authorize spend; run the founder held-out set with both policies in founder-v2 or founder-v2-hosted, review it blind, then compare. If the report says promote, change DEFAULT_PLANNING_POLICY in a reviewed pull request that carries it.

review.result: An independent code review found 3 blocking and 10 smaller issues, two of them pre-existing, plus suggestions. All are fixed in b050b6f8; each guarantee has a test that fails when it is removed (55 of 55).
blocking: C1: the unnecessary-AI check counted only what each policy composed and ran, so a candidate abstaining on a task scored as using less AI; one extra step also counted once per scenario
C2: 'frozen before the runs' rested on the rule file's own date; runs did not pin the rule, so a threshold edited after the results could change the verdict, and a run without a start time passed
T1: the prompt pin composed with no tools, roles, library or machines, so the prompt text production sends was not pinned
minor: an incomplete run reported keep_baseline, and --policy both ran the baseline half first (C3)
the not_worse option allowed promotion without the correction improvement the card requires (C4)
the report did not say which prompt version or runs it measured (C5)
float subtraction failed a drop exactly at the allowance (C6)
the tool-loop repair was not captured, and tool-loop system prompts were stripped of their rules (T2, T3)
four comparison clauses had no test: missed abstentions, the allowance, several profiles, the automatic measure (T4)
the doc's exit codes omitted incomplete (D1)
pre-existing: the evaluation composed without roles or library (P1); refusals printed local paths (P2)
suggestions_taken: interleave the two policies task by task
a direct composer call follows the selector
warn once per rejected value until a valid read, and log the policy and its source when they change
say in the pin test that the catalog's event types are part of what the composer is shown
